entries.test: Whether a system widely accepted as AGI emerges without having demonstrably solved abstraction, compositionality and the type-token distinction.
entries.note: The drafter's second condition (pictures and conversation don't need these solved) is context, not an antecedent. 'AGI' and 'solving' are loose terms, but the necessity claim has a plain reading.

entries.test: Whether the cited compositionality study reports that modern architectures fail at compositional generalization in the way early-1990s networks did.
entries.note: The abstract was an embedded image and the study isn't named in the text, so it has to be identified from the original post.

entries.test: Whether Mitchell's book and 'Stochastic Parrots' document limitations of current models that match problems identified in earlier neural networks.
entries.note: The claim is hedged ('some of', 'help establish'), and the proposition keeps the hedges.

entries.test: Reporting on whether AI companies outsourced RLHF and data-labeling work to low-wage contract workforces by early 2023, e.g. the 2023 reports on OpenAI's contractors in Kenya.
entries.note: The 'not sure' part is a hedge. The firm, checkable part is the outsourcing of patching work to low-paid labor, and 'sweatshops' is loaded wording.
